newsitem.title: USA: Court issues $30 mln verdict in Honda case - WSJ
newsitem.headline: Court issues $30 mln verdict in Honda case - WSJ

text.p: A district court jury has issued a $30 million verdict against Honda in the case of a 10-year-old driver killed after his Honda all-terrain vehicle flipped over, the Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The boy's parents filed the wrongful death-product liability suit after the February 19, 1995, accident, alleging that the "Big Red" three-wheel vehicle their son was driving was defective, the paper said.
A district court in Brownsville, Texas, found Honda auto-maker one-third liable and the boy's parents each one-third liable, the newspaper said.

A Honda spokesman told the Journal the company disagrees with the decision, because Texas legislation dictates that a plaintiff may only recover damages for negligence if his own responsibility does not exceed 60 percent.
The spokesman told the paper Honda believes there will be no payment under Texas law since the parents together were found 66-2/3 percent responsible.
The judge has not entered a judgment on the jury's verdict, and Honda decined to comment on its plans should the judge rule in the parents' favour, the Journal said.
